title: Finding and keeping patient information
description: Records should be complete, accessible and organised without dependence on one person.

questions.A1: How reliably can you find a returning patient's complete file within two minutes, even when the person who normally handles files is absent?
questions.A2: How consistently do you check that a new patient's required details are complete before the first treatment begins?
questions.A3: How consistently do you check for an existing patient file before creating a new one?
questions.A4: How reliably can the treating doctor find the patient's latest medical report without searching through separate messages or loose papers?
questions.A5: How consistently do you check that files used during the day have been returned to their correct place?

title: Keeping treatment connected between visits
description: Notes should help the treating doctor follow goals, changes and progress across visits.

questions.B1: How consistently is the patient's treatment goal written clearly enough to review at a later visit?
questions.B2: How consistently are treatment notes completed before the patient's visit is considered finished?
questions.B3: How reliably can another treating doctor understand what was done at the previous visit from the written record alone?
questions.B4: How consistently are changes to the patient's exercises or treatment recorded so the next visit follows the updated plan?
questions.B5: How consistently is the patient's progress reviewed against the treatment goal at the review point chosen by the treating doctor?

title: Knowing what was charged and collected
description: Invoices alone do not confirm that charges, collections and pending payments are complete.

questions.C1: How consistently do you check that every visit requiring payment has a charge recorded?
questions.C2: How consistently are payments entered into the patient's payment record on the day they are received?
questions.C3: How reliably can staff explain a patient's pending amount using the payment record, without relying on memory?
questions.C4: How consistently do you compare the day's recorded payments with the money actually received?
questions.C5: How consistently do you review pending patient payments on a fixed day each week?

title: Running the clinic without constant owner involvement
description: Clear responsibility and repeatable routines should reduce dependence on constant intervention.

questions.D1: How consistently is one person clearly responsible for checking that the day's patient records are complete?
questions.D2: How reliably can routine reception work continue when the usual receptionist or assistant is absent?
questions.D3: How consistently do you review patients who stopped attending before their planned treatment was completed?
questions.D4: How reliably can you obtain an accurate weekly count of completed treatment visits without counting individual entries yourself?
questions.D5: How consistently do you check that a clinic problem identified earlier has actually been corrected?

title: Protecting patient records and preparing for interruptions
description: Protect access to records and check whether recovery arrangements actually work.

questions.E1: How consistently are patient files kept where visitors and other patients cannot read them?
questions.E2: How consistently do you check that only the appropriate staff can access patient records?
questions.E3: How reliably do you keep a separate, protected copy of important records in case the originals are lost or damaged?
questions.E4: How confidently can you recover a sample patient record from that separate copy, based on a check you have actually performed?
questions.E5: How consistently do you check that a person leaving the clinic has returned clinic records and no longer has access to them?
